outcome: Explain what algorithms are and that programs run by following precise, unambiguous instructions on digital devices.
Use logical reasoning to predict what simple programs will do.
Use technology purposefully to create, organise, store, change and find digital content.
Recognise common uses of information technology beyond school.
Use technology safely and respectfully, keep personal information private and know where to get help with online concerns.
Design, write and debug programs for specific goals, including controlling or simulating physical systems.
Solve problems by breaking them into smaller parts.
Use sequence, selection and repetition in programs.
Work with variables and different forms of input and output.
Use logical reasoning to explain how simple algorithms work and to find and fix errors.
Describe computer networks, including the internet, the services they offer such as the web, and how they help communication and collaboration.
Use search technologies well, understand how results are selected and ranked, and judge digital content critically.
Select, use and combine software and internet services to create programs, systems and content, including collecting, analysing, evaluating and presenting data.
Use technology safely, respectfully and responsibly, recognise acceptable and unacceptable behaviour, and know ways to report concerns.
